rubric.note: Subjective internal editorial ratings with evidence; not an automatic humour metric or an independent live review.

card.title: Formerly Important
card.instruction: Carry the habits and expectations of a role that once made you important, even when the present no longer supports them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've brought my headteacher's bell to the retirement lunch. Shall I ring everyone into their seats?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please sit down. I promised the caterers we'd start at one.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then give me the register. I'll find who's holding us up.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's a buffet. Your former colleagues can serve themselves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll appoint table monitors. They can report to me before anyone takes seconds.

card.title: Formerly Important
card.instruction: Carry the habits and expectations of a role that once made you important, even when the present no longer supports them.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Bring the shop takings over. I've put out my counting tray.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You sold me the shop last year. I count them now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Bring your total and I'll check it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I came to invite you to our anniversary sale.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Already a year? Leave me the proposed discounts. I'll approve them before you print.

card.title: One Mistake from Gone
card.instruction: Treat every decision as a test of whether you still deserve your place.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First lunch as supervisor. If I order soup, will they think promoting me was a mistake?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I promoted you. I'm having soup.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then soup. Unless copying you proves I can't lead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Choose mine too. I need to take this call.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Both lunches? Right. Does choosing the bread count toward whether I keep the job?

card.title: One Mistake from Gone
card.instruction: Treat every decision as a test of whether you still deserve your place.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've signed for the delivery. Does that look like someone who should still be warehouse manager?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm the driver. You signed in my box. Use the manager box.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Already doing someone else's job. Should I hand back my keys?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: First, accept or refuse the damaged pallet. I need to leave.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Could you witness why I deserve to make that decision before I sign?

card.title: Chosen by Power
card.instruction: Seek the attention of whoever seems influential and treat that attention as proof that you belong.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The mayor said hello. That means I can sit at her table, doesn't it?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm seating donors. She says hello to everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Introduce me again. If she remembers me, you'll know I belong there.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: She's asked you to bring over that empty chair.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: She picked me. I'll carry it over and ask which side of her I should sit.

card.title: Chosen by Power
card.instruction: Seek the attention of whoever seems influential and treat that attention as proof that you belong.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put me beside the director in the group photo.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm photographing her team. She only asked you to hold her coat.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell her my name. She should know who she's trusting.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Now she wants you to hold her bag. I need your hands free for the photo.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Skip my photo. Ask her whether I should bring both to her next meeting. She clearly needs me on the team.

card.title: Power Vacuum
card.instruction: Treat any uncertainty about who is in charge as an emergency that must be resolved immediately.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Nobody's chairing this picnic. We can't open the hamper.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We can decide together. I just want everyone fed before the games.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Together isn't a name. The children are opening crisps—who can tell them to wait?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Fine, you're in charge of lunch. Sam's running the games.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stop his whistle. Who's in charge if a game runs into lunch? We need one name now.

card.title: Power Vacuum
card.instruction: Treat any uncertainty about who is in charge as an emergency that must be resolved immediately.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The manager's gone. Wait—who's in charge of the kettle?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Anyone. I'll make tea while you lock up.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then you're in charge. I'll tell everyone before I touch the doors.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only until my taxi comes. It's outside.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Name your replacement before you get in. We can't have boiling water between administrations.

card.title: Who Can Authorize This?
card.instruction: Treat titles and speeches as secondary; focus on who can grant access, allocate resources, and create consequences.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely ribbon-cutting. Our freezer delivery is outside; who can unlock the building?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The chief executive wants us both in the photograph first.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Can she let the freezers in? Photograph us while she unlocks.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Only the caretaker has keys. He's leaving in her car.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep her posing, then. I'll get the caretaker to open up before she needs her car.

card.title: Who Can Authorize This?
card.instruction: Treat titles and speeches as secondary; focus on who can grant access, allocate resources, and create consequences.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your title's impressive. Can you release the repair funds?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: My deputy handles finance.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then may I speak to the powerful part of this office?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I make the big decisions.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Good. Decide to introduce me to the cheque book.

transfer.action: I ring the bell from my former office beside {prop}.
transfer.opening: This used to come to my desk first. {request}
transfer.response: The title changed, not my judgement. {counter}
transfer.challenge: You don't hold that office now.
transfer.closing: The bell has remained admirably consistent about where it points.

transfer.action: I erase my first answer beside {prop} and hesitate over the pen.
transfer.opening: This needs to prove they chose me correctly. {request}
transfer.response: I'd rather check once than lose the chair over it. {counter}
transfer.closing: Small enough for a mistake to look entirely my fault.

transfer.action: I position {prop} beside the grandest nameplate.
transfer.opening: An introduction from you would change things. {request}
transfer.response: Make sure they know I was personally invited. {counter}
transfer.closing: Yes, but some invitations sound much closer to the centre.

transfer.action: I put a responsible-person box beside {prop}.
transfer.opening: We cannot leave that box empty. {request}
transfer.response: Someone must occupy the deciding chair. {counter}
transfer.closing: Who signs the decision made by all?

transfer.action: I put a requisition beside {prop}, ignoring the ceremonial banner.
transfer.opening: Lovely title. Who actually releases the funds? {request}
transfer.response: Show me the signature that opens the door. {counter}
transfer.closing: Did the speech unlock anything we can use?
